stanzas.sanskrit:
यत्नेषु सर्वेष्वपि नावकेशी
केशी स भोजेशितुरिष्टबन्धुः ।
त्वं सिन्धुजाऽवाप्य इतीव मत्वा
सम्प्राप्तवान् सिन्धुजवाजिरूपः ॥ ७१-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Keshi, a close friend of Kamsa was always successful in all of his attempts. He took the form of a horse and started from the land of Sindhu, thinking to himself, Krishna is easily accessible to Mahalakshmi who came out of Sindhu ocean.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yatneṣu sarveṣvapi nāvakeśī
keśī sa bhojeśituriṣṭabandhuḥ |
tvaṃ sindhujā’vāpya itīva matvā
samprāptavān sindhujavājirūpaḥ || 71-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
गन्धर्वतामेष गतोऽपि रूक्षै-
-र्नादैः समुद्वेजितसर्वलोकः ।
भवद्विलोकावधि गोपवाटीं
प्रमर्द्य पापः पुनरापतत्त्वाम् ॥ ७१-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Though this asura took the form of celestial horse, his fierce voices frightened the three worlds and went attacking the people of Gokula. Finally he came and stood in front of Krishna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
gandharvatāmeṣa gato’pi rūkṣai-
-rnādaiḥ samudvejitasarvalokaḥ |
bhavadvilokāvadhi gopavāṭīṃ
pramardya pāpaḥ punarāpatattvām || 71-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तार्क्ष्यार्पिताङ्घ्रेस्तव तार्क्ष्य एष
चिक्षेप वक्षोभुवि नाम पादम् ।
भृगोः पदाघातकथां निशम्य
स्वेनापि शक्यं तदितीव मोहात् ॥ ७१-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Keshi kicked the chest of Sri Krishna, whose legs are kept on Garuda, with his hooves. Having heard the story of Sage Bhrigu kicking Bhagwan on his chest, Keshi thought foolishly, even he can do so.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tārkṣyārpitāṅghrestava tārkṣya eṣa
cikṣepa vakṣobhuvi nāma pādam |
bhṛgoḥ padāghātakathāṃ niśamya
svenāpi śakyaṃ taditīva mohāt || 71-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
प्रवञ्चयन्नस्य खुराञ्चलं द्रा-
-गमुं च चिक्षेपिथ दूरदूरम् ।
सम्मूर्छितोऽपि ह्यतिमूर्छितेन
क्रोधोष्मणा खादितुमाद्रुतस्त्वाम् ॥ ७१-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna caught and took the horse by its hooves and threw him far. Keshi fainted but then rushed back with more anger and fury.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
pravañcayannasya khurāñcalaṃ drā-
-gamuṃ ca cikṣepitha dūradūram |
sammūrchito’pi hyatimūrchitena
krodhoṣmaṇā khāditumādrutastvām || 71-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वं वाहदण्डे कृतधीश्च बाहा-
-दण्डं न्यधास्तस्य मुखे तदानीम् ।
तद्वृद्धिरुद्धश्वसनो गतासुः
सप्तीभवन्नप्ययमैक्यमागात् ॥ ७१-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Deciding to punish the horse, Krishna kept HIS arm in to its mouth. The arm grew in size and choked Keshi to death. Though he was a demon in the form of horse, he became one with Bhagwan immediately.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvaṃ vāhadaṇḍe kṛtadhīśca bāhā-
-daṇḍaṃ nyadhāstasya mukhe tadānīm |
tadvṛddhiruddhaśvasano gatāsuḥ
saptībhavannapyayamaikyamāgāt || 71-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
आलम्भमात्रेण पशोः सुराणां
प्रसादके नूत्न इवाश्वमेधे ।
कृते त्वया हर्षवशात् सुरेन्द्रा-
-स्त्वां तुष्टुवुः केशवनामधेयम् ॥ ७१-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Indra and all other Gods were happy at the killing of the horse and considered it to be equivalent to Ashwamedha sacrifice done by Krishna. They gave Krishna with name, "Keshava" meaning killer of Keshi and sang his glory.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ālambhamātreṇa paśoḥ surāṇāṃ
prasādake nūtna ivāśvamedhe |
kṛte tvayā harṣavaśāt surendrā-
-stvāṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ keśavanāmadheyam || 71-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कंसाय ते शौरिसुतत्वमुक्त्वा
तं तद्वधोत्कं प्रतिरुध्य वाचा ।
प्राप्तेन केशिक्षपणावसाने
श्रीनारदेन त्वमभिष्टुतोऽभूः ॥ ७१-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Sage Narada introduced Krishna as son of Vasudeva to Kamsa and later prevented Kamsa from killing Vasudeva. At the end of Keshi Vadham, Narada met Krishna and sang his glory.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kaṃsāya te śaurisutatvamuktvā
taṃ tadvadhotkaṃ pratirudhya vācā |
prāptena keśikṣapaṇāvasāne
śrīnāradena tvamabhiṣṭuto’bhūḥ || 71-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कदापि गोपैः सह काननान्ते
निलायनक्रीडनलोलुपं त्वाम् ।
मयात्मजः प्राप दुरन्तमायो
व्योमाभिधो व्योमचरोपरोधी ॥ ७१-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: One day Krishna was playing hide and seek with Gopas in the forest. At that time, son of Mayan, Vyoman who has immense magical powers approached Krishna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kadāpi gopaiḥ saha kānanānte
nilāyanakrīḍanalolupaṃ tvām |
mayātmajaḥ prāpa durantamāyo
vyomābhidho vyomacaroparodhī || 71-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
स चोरपालायितवल्लवेषु
चोरायितो गोपशिशून् पशूंश्च ।
गुहासु कृत्वा पिदधे शिलाभि-
-स्त्वया च बुद्ध्वा परिमर्दितोऽभूत् ॥ ७१-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Gopas were playing thief and police, when Vyomasura acted as thief in the game and hid the cows and gopas in a cave and closed its entrance with a stone. Krishna understood the situation and killed him and freed the cows and gopas.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sa corapālāyitavallaveṣu
corāyito gopaśiśūn paśūṃśca |
guhāsu kṛtvā pidadhe śilābhi-
-stvayā ca buddhvā parimardito’bhūt || 71-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
एवंविधैश्चाद्भुतकेलिभेदै-
-रानन्दमूर्छामतुलां व्रजस्य ।
पदे पदे नूतनयन्नसीमां
परात्मरूपिन् पवनेश पायाः ॥ ७१-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna made Vraja a happy place for the gopas with his amazing actions. Bhattathiri prayed to that supreme Bhagwan who made the people of Vraja happy, to protect him from his afflictions.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
evaṃvidhaiścādbhutakelibhedai-
-rānandamūrchāmatulāṃ vrajasya |
pade pade nūtanayannasīmāṃ
parātmarūpin pavaneśa pāyāḥ || 71-10 ||
